metadata.title: One Config Sheet, No Code Edits
metadata.note: Week 5 progress report. Voice hai/Bella for @HumanitariansAI. Content only from the later stages of the visual tracker chat; no claim that the sheet is live.
metadata.author: Risa Samanta

beats.narration_text: A tracker only helps if the team can change it without touching code. This is Risa Samanta's progress report for the week: making the visual tracker run from one Config sheet.

props.command: claude "make the tracker reusable: every setting the team might change lives on one Config sheet, no code edits"
output: no code edits to change a status

beats.narration_text: The Config sheet holds everything the team might change: the statuses and their colors, the team names and emails, the visual types, the chapters, and the column names on the Data sheet, plus a link to each chapter's CAJAL document. The script reads them from there, so changing a status is an edit to a cell, not to code.

props.title: the Config sheet
props.code:
Config
  statuses + colors
  team names + emails
  visual types
  chapters
  column names on Data
  CAJAL link for each chapter
props.sparkLine: Change a cell, not the code.

beats.narration_text: A tracker like this breaks quietly, so there is a checker. Check for problems looks for duplicate names on Config, a status with no color, an email that does not look right, and values on the Data sheet that are not on any Config list, like a misspelled status left over from the old sheet.

props.command: claude "write a checker that reports anything on the Data sheet that is not on a Config list"

beats.narration_text: Switching the live sheet over took five steps. Import the new workbook and replace the spreadsheet, replace the three updated script files, run set up and repair, run the problem check, then create a filter view for each person. The original Excel file stays as a backup until everyone has used the new sheet for about a week.

props.title: switching the live sheet over
props.code:
1. File > Import > Replace spreadsheet
2. Replace Config, Validate and Alerts in Apps Script
3. Tracker > Set up / repair tracker
4. Tracker > Check for problems
5. Tracker > Create a filter view for each person

# keep the original Excel file as a backup

beats.narration_text: One fix mattered. The script had assumed two status names, Needs Review and Published, but the team's words are In Review and Done. Config, Validate and Alerts were updated to read those two names from the sheet, so the checker and the email alerts follow the team's wording.
beats.visual_intent: Real drifted caption names from the actual repo animating toward a clean sectioned scheme. Show the mechanism, not a count.

lines.text: the team's words: In Review / Done

props.caption: read the names from Config, do not assume them

beats.narration_text: The point is reuse. Make a copy of a working tracker and the script comes with it. Replace the statuses, team, types and chapters on Config, run setup, run the checker. No code changes are needed, so the same tracker can serve another project.

props.command: claude "how do I reuse this tracker for another project?"

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you build a tracker for your own team, put every setting on one Config sheet, and ask Claude to write a checker that reports anything on the data sheet that is not on a Config list. Then run the checker after every import.

props.command: claude "put every setting on one Config sheet, and write a checker for anything on the data sheet that is not on a Config list"

beats.narration_text: One Config sheet, no code edits. This has been Risa Samanta's report, voiced by Bella for Humanitarians AI. Run the checker after every import.
